civilopediaText.text: The five layers of power
A cultivator's body alone is weak: most of its power comes from its Gu, its dao marks and its comprehension of its path. One who fights without Gu still fights, on dao marks and comprehension alone.

1. Rank. The body's strength: Rank One 6, Rank Two 10, Rank Three 14, Rank Four 21, Rank Five 29, Rank Six 36, Rank Seven 51, Rank Eight 69, the Venerable 168. Clan Masters of a rank have the same strength. Mortal and immortal are two worlds: an immortal fights mortal units 50% harder, the Venerable 100% harder.

2. Path attainment (comprehension). Four tiers stack: Master +20% at any rank, Grandmaster +25% from rank three, Great Grandmaster +30% from rank six, Supreme Grandmaster +35% from rank eight: +110% at the top. Each tier opens a new kind of power: the Master the path's hit on every attack it makes, the Grandmaster a second effect and the mortal killer move, the Great Grandmaster a domain or a new art and the immortal killer move, the Supreme Grandmaster the path's peak.

3. Dao marks, the quantity of dao. Tiers I to V give +10%, +20%, +30%, +40% and +10 HP healing, +55% and +15 HP healing. Every tier also raises the path's hit: extra damage 4/5/6/8/10/12, status turns 2/2/2/3/3/4, healing 5/6/8/10/12/15, XP 2/3/4/5/6/8, stolen stones 10/15/20/25/30/40%, movement 1/1/1/1/2/2 (no marks, then I to V; a path may multiply them). The Master's promotion lists what each tier adds.

Dao marks grow one tier every 20 turns on Standard for a path Master of rank three or more; an immortal also gains one for every immortal it kills and every heavenly tribulation it survives. Mortals stop at tier II. Rank seven needs tier II, rank eight tier III, the Venerable tier IV.

4. Gu. Each path's Gu comes with its Master. A Master refines more with XP: 113 catalog Gu of ranks 1 to 9, each waiting for a unit of its rank; a Gu's effect grows with its rank (a rank-one attack Gu +12%, a rank-nine one +44%). Immortal Gu sleep while the clan has no immortal essence of their rank. Every immortal Gu wonder of your own path that your clan owns adds 5% strength; one of a strongly clashing path takes 5% away. Spoils: a Gu Master that defeats a unit takes each of its catalog Gu of rank 1 to 5 with a 25% chance, when its own rank can hold it.
5. Conflicts. A second path whose dao marks clash with the first costs 5% to 25% strength.
Killer moves

A unit-action button: for one turn the path family's burst plus the path's hit at full power (twice that for the immortal move). The mortal move costs 15 stones; the immortal move costs the immortal's own essence: 5 green grape at rank six, 4 red date at seven, 3 white lychee at eight, 2 yellow apricot as a Venerable. AI clans use these moves by themselves whenever they attack and can pay; they keep 100 stones and 10 essence in reserve, and a Venerable keeps its yellow apricot for Eternal Life.
Example

A Rank Six fire-path Great Grandmaster with Dao Marks III: strength 36, +75% from attainment and +30% from dao marks. Each attack inflicts Burning for 3 turns; each attack deals 6 extra damage; domain: enemies beside it fight 10% weaker.
Every rank has four small stages: initial, middle, upper and peak. A Gu Master climbs them by cultivating; each stage above initial adds 5% Strength.
One stage every 8 turns with grade A aptitude, 10 with B, 12 with C, 16 with D and 5 with an extreme physique (Standard speed; the other speeds scale). An immortal takes 2 times as long.
A new rank starts again at initial. The breakthrough costs 30% fewer stones from the peak and 50% more before it.

Relic Gu, one colour for each mortal rank, bought with XP and primeval stones (green copper 25, red iron 40, white silver 60, yellow gold 90, purple crystal 130): it lifts the unit one stage at once and is spent.

An extreme physique: 1 awakening in a hundred. +20% Strength, +50% XP from combat, 20% less upkeep. After 60 turns (Standard speed) the aperture bursts and the unit dies, unless it has ascended to rank six.
How long an immortal lives

A clan's Lifespan Gu are its immortals' lifespan. Reaching each rank adds to the stock and a higher rank burns it more slowly, so every rank climbed makes an immortal live longer. Numbers on Standard speed; the other speeds scale the turns.
Rank six: +20 Lifespan Gu on ascending; burns one every 10 turns, so its own gift lasts about 200 turns.
Rank seven: +25 Lifespan Gu on advancing; burns one every 15 turns, so its own gift lasts about 375 turns.
Rank eight: +35 Lifespan Gu on advancing; burns one every 20 turns, so its own gift lasts about 700 turns.
The Venerable: +60 Lifespan Gu on becoming a Venerable; burns one every 30 turns, so its own gift lasts about 1800 turns.
All the clan's immortals share one stock, each burning at its own rank's rate. With none left an immortal wastes away (7 damage a turn) and heals only by pillaging; one Lifespan Gu ends that at once.
How to add lifespan
1. Climb. Every rank reached adds Lifespan Gu (above): the surest way.
2. Green land. From Calamity Lore, every 8 owned forest, jungle or marsh tiles of each kind give one with a 15% chance each turn: keep your woods and swamps, settle near them.

3. Immortal Gu and inheritances: Year Gu gives 1 every 3 turns; Years Flow Like Water gives 2 every 5 turns for 10 green grape essence while the clan holds more than 9; Red Lotus Inheritance gives 1 every 5 turns.
4. The market. Treasure Yellow Heaven sells 3 Lifespan Gu for 120 stones.
5. Conquest. A captured city keeps its immortal Gu and inheritances, so the ones above can be seized.
What takes lifespan
Wisdom Gu: takes 1 every 5 turns.
While a Venerable lives, every clan loses one each 10 turns.
The Zombie Alliance's immortals never age (it gains one per immortal each 10 turns) but make no essence.
Immortals against mortal clans

An immortal outclasses any mortal army: strength 36, 51 and 69 at ranks six to eight against 29 at rank five, before its path, and it crosses the region walls. That is the reward for a long, hard climb: ascension needs a rank-five Master, the three qi and luck, and every rank above needs a survived tribulation, dao marks and essence.

name: Gu World: Gu Hunger and Food

civilopediaText.text: Every Gu eats

A Gu that eats a Gu food (moon orchid, wild boar, jade or wine) takes it from the clan's stock every turn. When the clan is short, every Gu eating that food is weakened at once and its hunger meter rises each turn: a status on the unit shows the percent. At 100% the Gu rolls its chance to die, then the meter starts again. Feed the clan and the meter clears.
A path's own Gu is its Master's vital Gu: if it starves to death, the Master takes 30 damage (none at 30 HP or less). Its Master brings it back once the food is in surplus again.

Hunger rate by rank: rank 1 +33% a turn (50% death chance at 100%), rank 2 +20% a turn (50% death chance at 100%), rank 3 +14% a turn (50% death chance at 100%), rank 4 +11% a turn (50% death chance at 100%). The lower the rank, the faster the hunger.
Where the food comes from: moon orchid and wild boar from their improved tiles and the Gu Feeding House, jade from mined jade, wine only from the Tavern.
Other Gu eat primeval stones: each raises its unit's upkeep, usually by 10%. When the clan's stones fall below zero, every unit fights 20% weaker.
